Winter lawn care: keeping damage to a minimum

Use this simple checklist to help protect your lawn through winter in the North West.

1. Know when to stay off the grass
- Avoid walking on frosty grass where possible.
- Stay off waterlogged areas until the surface has started to firm up.
- If you must cross the lawn, try to use the same route rather than spreading foot traffic.

2. Keep on top of leaves and debris
- Remove the bulk of fallen leaves every week or two.
- Pay extra attention to shaded or damp corners where leaves sit longer.
- Lift toys, furniture and mats that block light and air from the grass.

3. Don’t panic about appearance
- It is normal for lawns to look tired, pale or patchy through winter.
- Focus on preventing compaction and waterlogging instead of chasing perfect stripes.
- Make a note of the worst areas so you can target them in spring.

4. Plan your spring work now
- Take photos of the lawn on wet days and after heavy use.
- Decide whether you’ll need scarifying, aeration, overseeding or just a feed.
- Book work early – spring slots can go quickly in dry spells.

If you’d like tailored advice for your lawn, we offer both on-site visits around Burnley and online design/maintenance consultations.
